hard_failures.finding: Declared-F0 vs F2b quantifier-domain divergence. research_map/formulation_taxonomy.yaml @0abb9ed8a961 (revision 5), classes.AF-SCC-C0-VAC-GEN.conclusion.text (line 346) reads 'For every admissible (s,delta) there is a comeager set G_{s,delta} of data ...'. schemas/af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml @55d0a1ea9bda (revision 12) defines quantifiers.domains.D0 (line 52) as 'a tagged disjoint union: r = smooth (the smooth-with-decay default) or r = (sobolev,s,delta) with s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1)' and quantifies 'forall r in D0' in quantifiers.formal (line 42) and conclusion.statement_formal (line 214). The declared F0 statement omits the smooth-with-decay branch that F2b treats as the default, so the two pinned artifacts state the same frozen class over different index domains. F2b f0_binding.declared_f0_sha256 equals the measured taxonomy hash, so the binding is hash-current but not index-consistent. F0 H3 ('the topology and weighted data spaces are owned by F2 and are unresolved here') makes this a dispositionable deferral, but the C0 conclusion text records no deferral and the lead's check_taxonomy_consistency.py compares taxonomy vs authoring supplement only, never the class-statement index domain, so its 'consistent: true' does not cover this axis.
hard_failures.falsifier: At the same pinned hashes: the finding is refuted if the taxonomy's C0 conclusion quantifies over the smooth-with-decay branch as well as the Sobolev branch, or if it carries an explicit index-deferral clause that supersedes its '(s,delta)' wording. A taxonomy hash change supersedes rather than falsifies it.

findings.finding: The same '(s,delta)' index pattern appears in the taxonomy's AF-SCC-C2-VAC-GEN conclusion (line 274), so W077-HF-01 is not F2b-specific; only the C0/F2b instance is adjudicated here.

F0 H3 explicitly defers the data space to F2 ('owned by F2 and are unresolved here') and genericity_value_status is provisional_owned_by_F2, which is why W077-HF-01 is filed as a dispositionable class-statement deferral (major) rather than a mathematical contradiction.

artifacts/formulation/tools/check_taxonomy_consistency.py compares research_map/formulation_taxonomy.yaml against the authoring supplement artifacts/formulation/formulation_taxonomy.yaml (axes/regularity/conclusion_type/exclusions/test cases/known_obstruction/genericity/data_class_freeze/transfer rules); it does not compare the quantified index domain of the class statements, so its 'consistent: true' output cannot license index consistency.

The classifier that produced W077-HF-01 is self-tested against five synthetic controls (equal r-index, omit-smooth, omit-sobolev, both-branches-named, absent index) and passes 5/5 before being applied to the real artifacts.
